newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates dip, bonds firm on cbank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates dip, bonds firm on cbank rate cut.

text.p: Greek depos and forwards eased on Friday after the central bank cut its overnight intervention bid, but bonds and the ecu/drachma held mostly steady, unaffected by a Salomon Brothers report. The central bank cut the intervention bid rate to 11.90 percent from 12.40 percent on Friday.

"The small downward adjustment of depo rates indicated the market had discounted this drop. Weekly rates lost 30 basis points and monthly rates 5.0 points. Two- and three-month rates were unaffected," said dealers at a state bank.
The forex forwards market had discounted a bigger drop in the overnight rate and as a result, managed to remain steady, dealers said.
Taxable bond prices gained 30 to 35 basis points and climbed another five basis points after the central bank's announcement.
The mark was quoted at 156.28/33 drachmas from Friday's 156.440 fix, the dollar at 263.16/26 drachmas from 263.730 and the Ecu at 303.60/70 from 303.890 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma did not fluctuate much. The Salomon Brothers report, which said the market would remain stable around at 305 in 1997, did not affect the market," forex dealers said.
